primitives.note: Overwhelm stacks store magic damage on the target (P); Golden Eclipse's damage scales with the number of Overwhelm stacks currently on the target (R).
Searing Brilliance stacks (gained 3 per ability cast, refresh, cap at 9, expire after 5s) arm Mel's next basic attack.
Mel's next basic attack after gaining Searing Brilliance stacks consumes all of them to fire that many extra magic-damage projectiles at the target.
Overwhelm's stored damage only detonates (bursts as a lump sum) once the accumulated post-mitigation stored damage would exceed the target's current health and shields.
Q's initial explosion, E's orb impact, and R's blast each deal a base + AP-scaled damage instance on cast/impact.
Q fires several bolts that each explode separately over a 0.5s channel; E's field ticks damage every 0.125s (reported per-tick at ~8 ticks/sec) after the orb lands.
Mana costs on Q/W/E/R (W's cost falls to 0 at rank 5) can matter for how many casts fit in the 15s window.

Rebuttal's shield and bonus move speed only affect damage taken/survival; its projectile-reflection damage cannot trigger in the damage fight since a stationary target dummy never fires projectiles at Mel.

needsBespoke.why: Overwhelm (Searing Brilliance passive) does not deal damage when a stack is applied; instead it adds to a stored-damage pool on the target that only bursts when a later stack's application would push the total post-mitigation stored damage above the target's *current* health and shields, at which point all stored damage releases at once (and the wiki flags a bug where 5 extra stacks are applied just before that consumption). Simulating this needs a running stored-damage ledger compared each hit against a shrinking health value and a delayed, conditional burst-release rule -- this is richer bookkeeping than target-stacks, execute-or-threshold, or conditional-damage alone can express, and their combination doesn't capture the 'burst happens on a *later* stack, not the one that crosses the line' timing.

unsettled.question: Which of the two mismatched value sets for R's Overwhelm scaling bonus is live: the wiki's stated increase (10/20/30 flat, 1/2/3 per stack) or the bin's MelR.BasePassiveFlatDamage/BasePassiveStackDamage rows (60/70/80 flat, 3/4/5 per stack)?
options: Wiki values (10/20/30 and 1/2/3) are the actual increase added on top of the base passive's own numbers
Bin values (60/70/80 and 3/4/5) are the live total passive stored-damage numbers once R is ranked
The two describe different things (total vs increase) and both are simultaneously correct once combined correctly

unsettled.question: When Overwhelm's stored damage would exceed the target's current health/shields, does the detonation happen on the very stack-application that crosses the threshold, or only on the next subsequent stack after that (per the literal wording 'the next stack applied ... will consume them all')?
options: Detonates immediately on the hit that pushes stored damage over the threshold
Detonates one damage-instance later than the threshold-crossing hit, per the literal wiki wording
The 'bug' note (5 extra stacks applied just before consumption) means detonation timing/amount is unreliable and should be modeled as instant with a flat +5-stack bonus
quotes: If the total {{tt|post-mitigation damage|Damage calculated after modifiers}} stored exceeds the target's {{as|'''current''' health}} and {{tip|shields}}, the next stack applied against them will consume them all to deal the stored damage.
Just before ''Overwhelm'' stacks are consumed, targets have 5 additional stacks applied to them.{{bug}}

unsettled.question: Do the bonus blazing projectiles fired by a Searing Brilliance-empowered basic attack each apply a separate Overwhelm stack (multiplying stack generation on that single attack), or does the whole empowered attack (base hit + all bonus projectiles) count as generating stacks only for the original attack's damage instance?
options: Every bonus projectile is its own damage instance and applies its own Overwhelm stack, in addition to the base attack's stack
Only the base attack applies an Overwhelm stack; the bonus projectiles are a bundled on-hit-like effect that doesn't independently stack Overwhelm
quotes: apply a {{tip|stack}} of ''Overwhelm'' for each instance of damage they deal to enemies
Effects that apply {{tip|on-hit|on-hits}} (e.g {{ii|Guinsoo's Rageblade}}) will not apply stacks.

proposal: Auto-attack the dummy to open, applying the first Overwhelm stack immediately.
Cast Q (Radiant Volley) on the dummy: its several explosions land as separate damage instances (each stacking Overwhelm) and the cast grants 3 Searing Brilliance stacks.
Cast E (Solar Snare) on the dummy next: the orb impact plus the ticking field add more damage instances and refresh Searing Brilliance to its cap of 9 (3+3, since it was already at 3).
Weave a basic attack in as soon as Searing Brilliance stacks are up, consuming them to fire bonus magic-damage projectiles at the dummy.

Cast R (Golden Eclipse) as soon as it is off cooldown and the dummy is Overwhelm-affected (true from the opening auto-attack onward); its damage scales with the dummy's current Overwhelm stack count, so ideally fire it right after a big stack-building sequence (Q+E+auto).
Repeat Q on cooldown (10s down to 6s by rank), E on cooldown (11s down to 9s), and basic attacks between casts for the remaining ~15s window, keeping Overwhelm and Searing Brilliance topped up.

Do not cast W (Rebuttal) for damage purposes: its only offensive component requires reflecting an enemy champion's projectile, and the stationary target dummy never casts anything at Mel, so W would only cost mana for a shield/move-speed effect that a pure damage-race dummy fight never needs.
questions: At what level and item/AP amount should the fight be run, given P's bonus-missile damage scales by champion level (not ability rank) while R's Overwhelm bonus scales by R's own rank -- do these need to be evaluated together at a fixed level/rank pairing (e.g. level 16, R rank 3)?

Should R be held back to maximize the Overwhelm stack count on the dummy for its per-stack bonus damage, or always cast on cooldown to also start its own long cooldown sooner, given the fight is only ~15s and R may only be castable once?

In a single-target dummy fight, do all of Radiant Volley's explosions reliably land on/near the dummy (given the 200-radius explosion vs 25-unit spread, distributed over a 250-unit combined area), or should the simulator assume some bolts might not connect against a single stationary hitbox?
